reconcile.note: Clarke revives the son-in-law theory, holding Joseph was Jacob's actual son per Matthew but became Heli's son-in-law by marrying Mary, whose line Luke instead records.

discrepancy.note: Strauss lays out how Matthew's Solomonic line and Luke's Nathan line diverge in nearly every name from David onward, starting with Joseph's own father.

quotes.text: In Matthew, the father of Joseph is called Jacob; in Luke, Heli. In Matthew, the son of David through whom Joseph descended from that king is Solomon; in Luke, Nathan: … Since this difference appears to offer a complete contradiction, the most industrious efforts have been made at all times to reconcile the two.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), pt. I, ch. IV, on Matthew 1:12 and Luke 3:27.
